source.title: Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability Evidence Does Not Survive Defensible Analytic Variation

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Page-break and layout artifacts do not prevent reading it.
record.tranche_reason: The study varies circuit-discovery specifications on GPT-2 small IOI and reports that the resulting circuits and mapped claims are unstable, challenging the robustness of circuit-level evidence. It also identifies conditions that affect the instability.
record.gate_note: The paper reports outcomes for discovered circuits, mapped claims, functional comparisons, and a random-circuit baseline. It does not directly test the original 26-head circuit's roles by head ablation or patching, or show that removing everything outside that original circuit changes IOI performance. The one failed discovery objective and the discard rates are reported, but are not circuit-result rows. Values used to select circuits or thresholds are not recorded as findings.
record.test_reason: On GPT-2 small IOI, the study runs a pre-registered multiverse of edge-attribution circuit discovery. It varies objective, ablation, corruption, metric, threshold, prompt variant and seed, and measures whether the discovered circuits agree. Mean Jaccard is 0.14 and the median pair shares 4% of edges. This directly tests whether different methods, ablations and metrics recover essentially the same circuit (V4). It compares specifications with each other, not with the original 26-head circuit.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that circuit-derived IOI claims on GPT-2 small are not filable: defensible analytic choices give near-disjoint, functionally uncorrelated circuits and contradictory claims (early vs late layers). Instability survives fixing any single axis and fixing circuit size. Size-matched discovered circuits beat a random null but remain too unstable. The authors also report that the pooled functional-gap result does not hold within sizes, and they limit the conclusion to one model and one task.
record.recipe_differences: Rather than testing the original 26-head circuit against its faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria, the paper runs a multiverse of edge-attribution circuit-discovery specifications using the Miller et al. library, maps circuits to Annex IV claims, and measures circuit and claim variation. It varies discovery objectives, ablation operators, corruption distributions, metrics, thresholds, prompt variants, and seeds.
record.method_sensitivity: Claim variation changes with analytic choices. Standardizing the evaluation metric reduces F most (0.1377); prompt variant removes 0.0084 and seed removes 0.0009. Holding circuit size fixed also changes comparisons with the random null and reduces the reported flip rate.

fits_no_version.finding: The derived Annex IV claim class (layer band and size class) flips on 73.2% of specification pairs. The study's filability criterion (modal share at least 1−α) fails at every tolerance and for all addressee and granularity combinations (Table 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Regulatory or documentation claims derived from circuit discovery are not reproducible across defensible analytic specifications.

record.problems: One model and one task are tested. The specification space is limited to the library rather than all defensible methods. One of seven discovery objectives fails on the canonical task, and 52.3% of specifications produce no circuit under the threshold rule, with discard rates uneven across metrics. The authors also state that bootstrap intervals are unusable for one reported family with very small conditioning groups.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported per-cell results were available to extract. The paper's claim-class tables, axis-standardization results, size-control comparisons, and functional-comparison results are represented above; individual specification-curve entries and the remaining size-stratified values in Table 7 are not separately recorded.

untested.parts: The 26-head, 7-class circuit and its faithfulness, completeness and minimality are not examined. Discovered circuits are edge sets that are never compared to it.
No name-mover ablation or backup-head analysis.
Only GPT-2 small on IOI. The Pythia-160m replication is pre-registered but not run.
Discovered circuits are compared with each other, not with the original circuit. Methods outside the Miller et al. library (e.g. optimal ablation, path patching) are not included.
How much of the model's IOI behaviour the original circuit explains, and how its faithfulness score shifts across ablations, are not measured.
There is no per-variant comparison of circuit components across name orders, templates or more names. ABBA/BABA enter only as a grid axis.

missing.what: Discard rate by evaluation metric under the metric-relative faithfulness threshold: comprehensiveness 0.003, KL 0.630, logit difference 0.679, sufficiency 0.779. This shows that whether circuits pass faithfulness depends on the metric.

Within-size flip rates (Table 7). Discovered circuits agree completely (F=0) at 5,000 and 10,000 edges, so 2,692 of 7,561 specifications contribute no flips. The instability sits below 2,000 edges, peaking at 0.58 at 100 edges.
Circuit accuracy rises with size from 0.51 to 0.95. Kappa stays at 0.016–0.047 across sizes, and the gap between functional and claim instability fails the threshold at 6 of 10 sizes.
Variance decomposition of circuit size: ablation×corruption 78.8%, ablation 4.4%, threshold 4.1%, metric 0.7%.

record.verdict_notes: V4 is challenged in an indirect sense. The study shows that library methods disagree with each other on edge-level circuits, which implies they cannot all recover the original circuit, but it never compares with Wang et al.'s heads. The reader's states were written relative to 'instability' rather than to the version's effect and have been re-scored against V4. V5 links on the claim-flip rows were dropped because those rows measure circuit and claim agreement, not faithfulness or completeness of a circuit. The single V5 verdict rests on the text (Table 2), which has no row; the gate note excluded discard rates as non-result rows. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test the original 26 attention heads, their seven stated classes or roles, or the original faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria.
No main-name-mover ablation or self-repair test is reported.
Only GPT-2 small on IOI is tested. Other models, sizes, checkpoints, tasks, and component reuse are not tested.
The study varies discovery objectives, ablation operators, metrics, and other specification choices, but does not compare every circuit-finding method or ablation type in the field.
The study measures variation in discovered circuits and mapped claims, not how much of the model's IOI behaviour remains after removing the circuit.
Although two prompt variants are included in the specification grid, the study does not report a prompt-specific comparison of circuit roles or test templates and prompts with more names.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Measured pairwise Jaccard similarity among discovered circuits across specifications.
rows.note: The study describes the circuits as almost disjoint; median pairwise Jaccard overlap is 4%.
rows.check: The state was scored as instability 'partial'. Against V4 (the same circuit is recovered), circuits are near-disjoint: mean Jaccard 0.1396, median about 0.04, only 1% of pairs above 0.8. Overlap is about 45 times chance, which the authors call not evidence of much.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Computed the flip rate of mapped Annex IV claims across the realized specification grid.
rows.note: The study says the flip rate clears its pre-registered threshold by more than three times.
rows.check: The derived claim differs on 73% of specification pairs, so different specifications do not yield the same circuit. The state should read against V4, not as 'instability observed'. This is a claim-map construct (layer band and size class), not faithfulness evaluation, so the V5 link is dropped.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Measured the modal share of mapped claims across the realized specification grid.
rows.note: The modal claim is well below the stated filability requirement.
rows.check: The modal claim covers only 41% of specifications, and the top two classes attribute IOI to early and late layers respectively. This bears on V4 agreement, not on V5 faithfulness sensitivity. The 0.80 filability requirement is the study's own criterion, not a baseline effect.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Recomputed claim flip rate within groups after standardizing the evaluation metric.
rows.note: Metric standardization removes 0.1377 from the flip rate, but the residual remains above the pre-registered threshold.
rows.check: With the metric held fixed, residual claim flip is 0.594, so the circuits still disagree. This is circuit agreement, not faithfulness evaluation; the V5 link is dropped.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Recomputed claim flip rate within groups after standardizing the ablation operator.
rows.note: The remaining flip rate is reported after holding the ablation operator fixed.
rows.check: With the ablation operator fixed, flip is still 0.70. The V5 link is dropped (no faithfulness score is measured).

rows.note: The remaining flip rate is reported after holding the discovery objective fixed.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Recomputed claim flip rate within groups after standardizing the prompt variant.
rows.note: The study reports that prompt standardization removes 0.0084 from F.
rows.check: With the prompt variant (ABBA/BABA) fixed, flip is still 0.72. Standardising prompt variant removes only 0.0084, but no per-variant circuit comparison is given, so V6 is not linked. The V5 link is dropped.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Recomputed claim flip rate within groups after standardizing the seed.
rows.note: The study says seed standardization removes 0.0009 from F; seeds select sampled prompts rather than nondeterminism.
rows.check: With the seed fixed, flip is still 0.73. The seed selects sampled prompts. The V5 link is dropped.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Removed circuit size from the mapped claim and held circuit size fixed in the within-group analysis.
rows.note: The study reports that the interval lower bound remains above the pre-registered threshold.
rows.check: The claim is reduced to layer band only, with size held fixed. Specifications then agree on 73% of pairs (flip 0.2706), still above the 0.20 threshold. This bears on V4 circuit agreement, not V5; the version link is changed.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Compared claim flip rates for the discovered multiverse and size-matched random null multiverses.
rows.measure: Claim flip rate, discovered versus random null
rows.uncertainty: Intervals disjoint; exact intervals not stated here
rows.note: The authors caution that the pooled direction is an artifact of the size distribution.
rows.check: This is the pooled comparison with a random null. The authors say its direction is an artefact of the size distribution (the null is degenerate above 1,000 edges) and do not report it as a finding.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Compared discovered-circuit and size-matched random-null claim flip rates with size held fixed.
rows.measure: Claim flip rate, discovered versus random null
rows.note: With size controlled, discovered circuits are more stable than the random null, but the authors say they remain too unstable to file.
rows.check: With size fixed, discovered circuits are more consistent than the random null (0.2746 vs 0.4230), but they still disagree on 27% of pairs.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Measured per-example functional agreement between pairs of discovered circuits.
rows.note: The paper also reports per-example agreement of 0.6028.
rows.check: Raw per-example agreement is 0.60, but the authors show it is largely explained by matching accuracy rather than by the same examples.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Measured Cohen's kappa for per-example functional verdicts from circuit pairs.
rows.note: The study characterizes the circuits as functionally uncorrelated by this measure.
rows.check: Kappa of 0.0146 means the circuits' per-example verdicts are essentially uncorrelated; they are not functionally interchangeable.

relationships.condition: GPT-2 small IOI, across the realized grid of discovery objectives, ablations, corruptions, metrics, thresholds, prompt variants and seeds (pooled and with any single axis fixed)
relationships.reason: Circuits are near-disjoint (mean Jaccard 0.14) and the derived claim differs on 73% of pairs (modal share 0.41). Flip stays at 0.59–0.73 with any single axis fixed, and per-example verdicts are uncorrelated at kappa 0.015 (r1–r10, r15).
relationships.display_finding: Mean circuit Jaccard was 0.14, derived conclusions differed across 73% of pairs, and the modal conclusion occupied 0.41 of specifications; fixing any single analysis axis left flip rates at 0.59–0.73, while per-example agreement had kappa 0.015.

relation.reason: The study measures agreement among discovered GPT-2 small IOI circuits across analytic specifications and metric-dependent threshold acceptance.

tranche.reason: Its own structural, functional and claim-agreement results contest V4 and establish metric sensitivity relevant to V5.

source_check.notes: Results cover one model and task, with 7,561 retained specifications and a 52.3% metric-imbalanced discard rate; bootstrap uncertainty is conditional on the grid. Statement checks assess only this study's contributions, not other studies or catalog-wide counts.

reader_labels.condition: GPT-2 small on IOI, across the realized specification grid
reader_labels.reason: Discovered circuits have low mean Jaccard similarity and high mapped-claim variation; their functional verdicts are also weakly associated (r1, r2, r15).

reader_labels.reason: Discovered circuits are more stable than random circuits when size is held fixed, although the authors report that the discovered circuits remain too unstable to file (r12, r13).

reader_labels.label: supports

reader_labels.reason: Standardizing each of these axes leaves substantial residual claim variation; standardizing the evaluation metric reduces it most but does not bring it below the stated threshold (r4-r8).
